patterns: Database class uses singleton factory pattern keyed by database:profile combination string. Each profile gets a named accessor method (getStagingInstance, getExtendedInstance, etc). Services construct Database instances in their constructors and hold them for lifetime. stagingExplorerService and stagingComparisonService both call getStagingInstance() in singleton constructors -- staging DB connection is attempted at module import time, not lazily. harvesterService uses a different staging access pattern: direct Database.getInstance(Config.DB_STAGING_DATABASE, Config.DB_STAGING_PROFILE) instead of getStagingInstance(). harvesterService implements self-disabling with stagingAvailable=false flag that starts false and permanently disables on first error. No other service follows this self-disable pattern.
dependencies: Staging subsystem chain: stagingRoutes.ts -> StagingExplorerService -> Database.getStagingInstance() -> Config.DB_STAGING_PROFILE (SERVER_PROFILE_2) -> SQL Gateway -> staging_PTRJ_iFES_Plantware. stagingRoutes.ts -> StagingComparisonService -> both getStagingInstance() + Database.getInstance(). harvesterService -> Database.getInstance(Config.DB_STAGING_DATABASE, Config.DB_STAGING_PROFILE) for Ffbscannerdata (dead path, stagingAvailable=false). Frontend: StagingComparisonPage, StagingDaftarUpahPage, StagingEmployeeDetailModal call /api/staging/* via stagingComparisonService.js.
integration_points: 1. Database.getStagingInstance() at db/client.ts:87-L89 -- primary staging access factory. 2. stagingRoutes.ts imports at index.ts:25 -- triggers staging service singleton construction at import time. stagingRoutes mounted at index.ts:285 (root) and index.ts:310 (proxy prefix). 3. HarvesterService at harvesterService.ts:419 and :494 -- direct Database.getInstance(Config.DB_STAGING_DATABASE, Config.DB_STAGING_PROFILE), bypassing getStagingInstance(). Dead code (stagingAvailable=false). 4. stagingComparisonService.test.ts -- integration tests connecting to real staging DB. 5. Frontend API calls through stagingComparisonService.js hitting /api/staging/* endpoints.
constraints: 1. DB_PROFILE and DB_STAGING_PROFILE both SERVER_PROFILE_2 -- staging and main db_ptrj share same server. 2. No DB_STAGING_DATABASE in backend/.env -- relies on config.ts default staging_PTRJ_iFES_Plantware. 3. DISABLE_STAGING_DB=true is dead config -- never parsed. Staging routes always active. 4. Staging service singletons constructed at import time (index.ts:25), not lazily -- connection failure blocks startup. 5. HarvesterService staging path disabled by in-memory flag stagingAvailable=false, not config. 6. STAGING_CATALOG constant duplicated in 3 files instead of using Config.DB_STAGING_DATABASE.

clarification_needs.question: Should DISABLE_STAGING_DB env var be wired up to actually gate staging API routes? Currently it exists in .env but is never read by any code.
clarification_needs.context: DISABLE_STAGING_DB=true is in backend/.env but Config class has no corresponding constant. Staging routes are always active regardless of this flag. If staging server is unreachable from current network, the staging API endpoints will fail at runtime.
options: Yes, wire DISABLE_STAGING_DB to conditionally skip mounting stagingRoutes in index.ts
No, keep staging routes always available and let them fail naturally if unreachable
Remove DISABLE_STAGING_DB from .env since it does nothing
Add staging health check that gates route mounting at startup
